chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Muhammad al-Wabishi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:

No believer dies in a land of exile, where those who would weep for him are absent, except that the regions of the earth upon which he used to worship Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, weep for him; his garments weep for him; the gates of heaven through which his deeds used to ascend weep for him; and the two angels entrusted with him weep for him.

key_terms.أَبْوَابُ ٱلسَّمَاءِ: the gates of heaven through which deeds ascend
key_terms.أَرْضِ غُرْبَةٍ: a land of exile or estrangement, away from one’s people
key_terms.بَوَاكِيهِ: those who would weep for him or mourn him
key_terms.بِقَاعُ ٱلْأَرْضِ: the tracts or places of the earth
key_terms.مُؤْمِنٍ: a believer, one distinguished by faith
key_terms.ٱلْمَلَكَانِ ٱلْمُوَكَّلَانِ بِهِ: the two angels assigned to and entrusted with him

ai.seo_question: What happens when a believer dies alone in a foreign land according to Imam Abu Abdullah عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that a believing servant’s worship leaves traces that are recognized beyond human society. If a believer dies far from family and mourners, the earth, his garments, the gates of heaven, and the angels appointed over him mourn him, showing the honor of faithful worship before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
